Amorphous

uh-MOR-fus -- stress on the second syllable, MOR. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Amorphous is without defined shape or form.

The jellyfish drifted past like an amorphous ghost, its edges impossible to trace in the dark water.

Worked Example

A lava lamp's glowing wax rises and falls, stretching, splitting, and merging, never holding a single outline for more than a second.

The wax is amorphous: it has no defined shape or form, only an endless flow from one blob to the next. Amorphous works for ideas too -- an amorphous plan is one that has never taken clear shape.

How Amorphous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

shapeless

shapeless: having no definite shape

nebulous

nebulous: hazy, vague, and ill-defined

formless

formless: entirely without form or structure

Antonyms

defined

defined: having clear form, limits, or outline

structured

structured: arranged in a clear, organized pattern

How Strong Is It? — nebulous → amorphous → formless

nebulous vs. amorphous

nebulous vs. amorphous: Nebulous is softer than amorphous -- a nebulous idea is merely hazy at its edges, while an amorphous one has no discernible shape anywhere at all.

formless vs. amorphous

formless vs. amorphous: Formless pushes even past amorphous: an amorphous cloud still has substance you can point to, while something formless lacks any form whatsoever, as if it could never hold a shape even for a moment.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of amorphous.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a-

prefix — a-: without; not (Greek a- (the 'alpha privative'))

root — morph

root — morph: form, shape (Greek morphe 'form')

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: full of; possessing the qualities of (Latin -osus, via Old French -ous)

Put it together

Put it together: Amorphous uses the -ous variant of this unit's suffix family -- but watch the reversal! Greek a- ('without') sits in front of morph ('form'), so instead of the usual 'full of' reading, amorphous literally means 'possessing the quality of having NO form.' The prefix flips the suffix's normal sense: this is the one word in the unit where -ous marks the fullness of an absence.

Use the root in a new word: metamorphosis

Use the root in a new word: metamorphosis: Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar completes its metamorphosis and emerges as a butterfly.

Root Check

Word Choice

Amorphous covers both the physical and the abstract: an amorphous blob of dough, but also an amorphous fear, an amorphous organization, an amorphous plan. Whenever something -- object or idea -- refuses to take a clear shape, amorphous is the word.
